capitals.note: 'Liu Zhang fortified within Chengdu' (200) and 'Yi Province's capital, Chengdu' (214); Liu Yan's earlier seat is not on the opened pages.

correction.text: Yi Province, 'covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing' (Liu Zhang page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 188-214; Cliopatria has no row and the Han shape (han-dynasty_184 to 214) keeps Yi Province inside it until 215. 'covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing'; the pages give no frontier and do not say whether the commanderies of Yunnan and Guizhou or Hanzhong (Zhang Lu's from 194) belonged to Yi. No infobox area on the pages.

region.text: Yi Province, 'covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing' (Liu Zhang page)

ledger.note: 188: Liu Yan takes Yi Province. 'Liu Yan was commissioned as the Governor of Yi Province' (End of the Han page, c. 188, in Emperor Ling's reforms); Liu Zhang followed him as Inspector c. 194 and Governor c. 194-214 (Liu Zhang page infobox).

region.text: Fu County, Luo and Chengdu, the road Liu Bei took into Yi Province

ledger.note: 213: Liu Bei's war in Yi. Invited by Liu Zhang in 211, 'in the spring of 213, Liu Zhang sent Liu Gui, Ling Bao, Zhang Ren, Deng Xian, Wu Yi and other officers to stop him at Fu'; 'In 214, Luo County fell to Liu Bei'.

region.text: Fu County, Luo and Chengdu, the road Liu Bei took into Yi Province

ledger.note: 214: Chengdu is surrounded and Liu Zhang surrenders: 'by 214 they had surrounded Yi Province's capital, Chengdu'; 'He then surrendered to Liu Bei' ('I don't want my subjects to suffer any more'). The End of the Han page dates the yielding to 215.

region.text: Yi Province, 'covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing' (Liu Zhang page)

ledger.note: 214: Yi Province passes to Liu Bei, who 'relocated him to Gong'an County in Jing Province' (Liu Bei page); the summary table: 'Defeated Liu Zhang and took over Yi Province' in 214.

region.text: Yi Province, 'covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing' (Liu Zhang page)

ledger.note: 214: Liu Zhang's Yi Province ends. Liu Bei 'succeeded Liu Zhang as the Governor of Yi Province'; Shu Han proper is proclaimed in 221.

wars.name: Liu Bei's conquest of Yi Province

zones.text: Fu County, Luo and Chengdu, the road Liu Bei took into Yi Province

wars.outcome: Liu Bei, invited in 211 against Zhang Lu, fought Liu Zhang from 213, took Luo in 214 and received the surrender of Chengdu.
wars.note: The Liu Bei page does not date the break with Liu Zhang; the End of the Han page puts the surrender in 215.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier for Yi Province; the shape is the two modern units the Liu Zhang page names.

sources.title: Liu Zhang (warlord)
sources.note: Inspector and Governor of Yi Province c. 194-214, covering present-day Sichuan and Chongqing; Zhao Wei 200; Liu Bei invited 211; surrender 214.

sources.title: End of the Han dynasty
sources.note: Liu Yan commissioned Governor of Yi Province c. 188; Liu Zhang yielded Yi to Liu Bei in 215.

sources.title: Liu Bei
sources.note: Spring 213 at Fu; Luo fell in 214; Liu Zhang surrendered and was moved to Gong'an in Jing Province.

notes:
Liu Zhang, Yi Province under Liu Yan and Liu Zhang 188-214. 3 pages opened (Liu Zhang (warlord), End of the Han dynasty, Liu Bei); no Cliopatria row. 'Liu Zhang' (the bare title) is a disambiguation page, the article is 'Liu Zhang (warlord)'.
Unsettled: (1) 214 (Liu Zhang and Liu Bei pages) against 215 (End of the Han page) for the surrender: 214 used; (2) 188 is 'c. 188' on the End of the Han page and Liu Yan's own page was not opened; (3) the Liu Zhang page gives Zhao Wei's revolt as 200 and the break with Zhang Lu as 'from this point on', no territory; (4) Hanzhong was an Yi Province commandery that Zhang Lu took in 194 with Liu Yan's nominal sanction: it is Zhang Lu's, not in this shape; (5) the south-west (Yunnan, Guizhou commanderies) is not on any page.
Counterparts: han-dynasty exists; shu-han is ea-03's (Cliopatria Shu Han 224..262); zhang-lu is written by this batch.
